t: Sejong, the fourth king of Joseon, reigned from 1418 to 1450 and is widely regarded as the greatest king in Korean history.

He is remembered above all for Hangul, the Korean alphabet published in 1446, and for a reign in which his court produced a native calendar, a rain gauge, vast medical and agricultural texts and new movable type.
He governed by Confucian principles and restricted Buddhist institutions while privately practising Buddhism, and North Korean histories stress the feudal burdens on the peasantry under his rule.
dyk: In 1430 Sejong had over 170,000 people polled on a proposed tax reform; the debate that followed lasted 17 years.
ev: Sejong's elder brother Yangnyŏng is deposed; Sejong becomes crown prince and then king when Taejong abdicates
Sejong launches the Ōei Invasion against Tsushima Island
Sejong re-establishes the Hall of Worthies
A campaign under Kim Chongsŏ against the Jurchens leads to six garrisons on the northern frontier
The rain gauge ch'ŭgugi is invented at court
The kongpŏp tax system is completed, lowering the land tax from 10% of the harvest to 5%
Hangul is published in the Hunminjeongeum and its commentary, the Hunminjeongeum Haerye
Sejong dies, the first Joseon king to die in office, and is succeeded by Munjong

f.born: 15 May 1397 (the 10th day, 4th month) in Chunsubang, Hanyang (Seoul); born Yi To, third son of Grand Prince Chŏngan, the future King Taejong, and Princess Chŏngnyŏng
f.died: 8 April 1450 (the 17th day, 2nd month), aged 52, after long illness, in the residence of Grand Prince Yŏngŭng in Gyeongbokgung; buried at Yeongneung
f.role: Prince Ch'ungnyŏng (1408), Grand Prince (1413), crown prince (1418); fourth king of Joseon, 1418–1450
f.known: The creation of Hangul and the Hunminjeongeum (1446); the Hall of Worthies; the rain gauge, water clock and Ch'ilchŏngsan calendar; the medical texts Hyangyakchipsŏngbang and Ŭibangyuch'wi; the kongpŏp tax reform; the Ōei Invasion of Tsushima and the northern frontier
